articles.title: Harvard SCoPEx: a small stratospheric measurement experiment, not a geoengineering deployment
articles.text: The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx) was a Harvard University scientific proposal to study how tiny amounts of aerosol particles behave in the stratosphere. Principal investigator Frank Keutsch and collaborators including David Keith described the concept publicly, including at the American Geophysical Union Fall Meeting in 2017. The experiment was designed to improve computer models used to estimate risks and benefits of solar geoengineering (solar radiation management). It was not a test of deploying geoengineering and was not intended to cool the planet. The planned platform was a scientific balloon gondola with propellers, flying near 20 km altitude. A very small amount of material — on the order of 100 grams to less than 2 kilograms, typically calcium carbonate (a common mineral found in limestone and used in products such as toothpaste) — would be released into a small mixed volume roughly 1 km long and 100 meters in diameter. The gondola would then fly back through that plume to measure aerosol microphysics, chemistry, and light scattering. A 2021 platform test in Sweden, planned with the Swedish Space Corporation from Esrange, was a hardware test only: the SCoPEx Advisory Committee recommended suspending it pending societal engagement, and no particles were to be released. In March 2024 Harvard announced that Keutsch was no longer pursuing SCoPEx; the platform is expected to be repurposed for stratospheric research unrelated to solar geoengineering.
questions: Was SCoPEx designed as a small scientific measurement experiment rather than a deployment of solar geoengineering to cool the planet?
Did the proposed science flight plan to inject thousands of tonnes of material into the stratosphere?
Was the proposed release typically calcium carbonate in amounts under 2 kilograms?
Did the 2021 Sweden platform test plan include releasing aerosols?
By 2024, had Harvard's principal investigator stopped pursuing SCoPEx?

articles.title: Chemtrails, SCoPEx, and Bill Gates: what the public scientific record shows
articles.text: The chemtrail conspiracy theory claims that long-lasting condensation trails behind high-flying aircraft are chemical or biological spraying for weather control, solar radiation management, or other hidden purposes. The scientific consensus is that this is false: persistent trails are ordinary contrails made of ice crystals that linger under certain humidity and temperature conditions. There is no evidence that purported chemtrails differ from normal water-based contrails. Debnath, Reiner, Sovacool and colleagues (iScience, 2023) analyzed 814,924 English-language tweets containing #geoengineering from 2009 to 2021. They found that chemtrails language dominates that discourse, that conspiracy narratives spill over across countries, and that Twitter volume surged around reporting on Harvard's SCoPEx project — including a peak near the April 2017 launch, on the order of 8,000 tweets. A consortium of funders supporting related solar geoengineering research included the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation; Bill Gates is a frequent target of conspiracy narratives. Funding climate or geoengineering research is not evidence of a covert aircraft spraying program. In the 2018–2021 window, Debnath et al. report that chemtrails talk became semantically broader, more toxic, and more tied to demands to stop alleged spraying, while a smaller stream of tweets discussed legitimate environmental concerns such as ozone, biodiversity, and mitigation.
questions: Does the scientific community treat chemtrails as a verified secret spraying program?
Are persistent aircraft trails explained as ordinary ice-crystal contrails under certain atmospheric conditions?
Did Debnath and colleagues analyze hundreds of thousands of #geoengineering tweets and find chemtrails conspiracy language dominant?
Did public #geoengineering Twitter activity surge around the SCoPEx project around April 2017?
Does Bill Gates funding climate or geoengineering research constitute evidence that aircraft are spraying chemicals for population control?

articles.title: The Paris Agreement: a 2015 treaty of nationally determined contributions, not a secret world government cap
articles.text: On 12 December 2015, parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change adopted the Paris Agreement at COP21. It is a legally binding international treaty that entered into force on 4 November 2016. The United Nations reports that 195 Parties (194 states plus the European Union) have joined. Article 2 sets the long-term temperature goal of holding the increase in global average temperature to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursuing efforts to limit the increase to 1.5°C. The Agreement does not assign each country a single, unchanging UN-imposed emissions quota. Instead, each Party prepares, communicates and maintains successive nationally determined contributions (NDCs) and is expected to submit an updated NDC every five years, with successive NDCs representing a progression of ambition. A global stocktake assesses collective progress; the first stocktake concluded at COP28 in 2023. The Agreement also addresses adaptation and climate finance for developing countries. Implementation depends on domestic measures and subsequent NDC cycles, not on a one-time secret pact that automatically stops warming.
questions: Was the Paris Agreement adopted at COP21 in Paris on 12 December 2015?
Does the Agreement aim to hold warming well below 2°C while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C?
Does Paris assign each country a single UN-imposed emissions quota that never changes?
Are Parties expected to communicate nationally determined contributions on a five-year cycle?
Did the treaty enter into force in November 2016?

articles.title: The 97% climate consensus: what Cook et al. and NASA actually measured
articles.text: Multiple independent lines of evidence show a strong scientific consensus that humans are causing recent global warming. NASA states that the vast majority of actively publishing climate scientists — 97 percent — agree that humans are causing global warming and climate change, and that leading science organizations including national academies and the IPCC have issued supporting statements. Cook et al. (2013, Environmental Research Letters) examined 11,944 abstracts from 1991–2011 matching 'global climate change' or 'global warming'. They reported that 66.4% of abstracts expressed no position on anthropogenic global warming, 32.6% endorsed it, 0.7% rejected it and 0.3% were uncertain. Among abstracts that expressed a position, 97.1% endorsed the consensus that humans are causing global warming; author self-ratings yielded 97.2% among papers that took a position. The well-known '97%' figure is therefore conditional: it is not a claim that 97% of all climate abstracts explicitly endorsed AGW, because a large share took no position in the abstract. It is also not a poll of the general public. Later syntheses (including Cook et al. 2016) find similarly high consensus among climate experts.
questions: Did Cook et al. 2013 find about 97% endorsement among abstracts that took a position on human-caused warming?
Did roughly two-thirds of the Cook et al. abstracts express no position on anthropogenic global warming?
Does NASA state that about 97% of actively publishing climate scientists agree humans are causing warming?
Does the 97% figure mean that 97% of all climate papers in that sample explicitly endorsed AGW in the abstract?
Have major science academies and the IPCC issued public statements that humans are causing climate change?

articles.title: Mountain glaciers: worldwide mass loss, not a story of global advance
articles.text: NOAA Climate.gov, reviewing World Glacier Monitoring Service (WGMS) data through the 2023/24 monitoring year, reports that worldwide most glaciers are shrinking or disappearing. Preliminary WGMS figures show 2023/24 was the 37th consecutive year that climate reference glaciers lost rather than gained ice. Cumulative loss since 1970 is equivalent to about 27.3 meters of water — roughly like removing 30 meters of ice from the entire surface of each glacier in that network. Ice loss has accelerated: NOAA cites decade-mean losses that were much larger in the 2010s than in the 1980s. Melting glaciers and ice sheets are a major cause of recent sea-level rise, and glacier retreat threatens summer water supplies in many regions. Local exceptions exist: tidewater glaciers can advance or retreat for geometric reasons even in a warming climate, and a given year can include a few positive mass balances. Those exceptions do not reverse the global signal. The IPCC assessment quoted by NOAA is that almost all of the world's glaciers retreating synchronously since the 1950s is unprecedented in at least the last 2,000 years.
questions: Have WGMS climate-reference glaciers lost mass for decades in a row through 2023/24?
Did IPCC assessment, as quoted by NOAA, treat near-synchronous glacier retreat since the 1950s as unprecedented in at least 2,000 years?
Does glacier science claim that every individual glacier on Earth is currently advancing?
Is melt of mountain glaciers and ice sheets a major contributor to recent sea-level rise?
Has ice loss in the reference network accelerated in recent decades compared with the 1980s?

articles.title: Polar bears and sea ice: habitat loss is the core threat, not a booming global population
articles.text: Polar bears (Ursus maritimus) hunt seals from sea ice; their seasonal biology is tied to spring ice retreat and autumn freeze-up. A NASA-funded study in The Cryosphere (Stern and Laidre, 2016) found a trend toward earlier sea-ice melt and later ice growth across all 19 polar bear subpopulation regions during 1979–2014. Ice-covered days declined on the order of 7 to 19 days per decade in most regions, with larger losses in the Barents Sea and central Arctic Basin. IUCN lists the polar bear as Vulnerable. A 2015 IUCN Red List reassessment identified loss of sea-ice habitat from climate warming as the most serious long-term threat and reported a high probability of a greater than 30% decline in global population over about 35–40 years. Subpopulation counts are incomplete and mixed: some units have been assessed as stable or increasing over short intervals, several are data-deficient, and habitat metrics have declined even where counts are uncertain. A slogan that 'polar bear numbers are growing' is therefore not a valid global summary. Habitat loss from sea-ice decline remains the central conservation issue.
questions: Do polar bears depend on sea ice as a hunting platform for seals?
Has satellite analysis found earlier spring melt and later autumn freeze-up across polar bear regions?
Does declining sea-ice habitat imply that every polar bear subpopulation has a published, increasing population count?
Has IUCN identified climate-driven sea-ice loss as the most serious long-term threat and listed polar bears as Vulnerable?
Is the claim that polar bear numbers are simply growing worldwide a well-supported summary of the evidence?

articles.title: CO2 is used by plants and is still a greenhouse gas: the plant-food slogan is not a climate disproof
articles.text: Carbon dioxide is a raw material for photosynthesis. NASA has reported that rising CO2 has contributed to a greening of parts of Earth's vegetated land via a CO2 fertilization effect. That fact does not cancel CO2's role as the principal long-lived greenhouse gas driving recent warming. NASA's Earth Observatory carbon-cycle explainer notes that extra atmospheric CO2 also dissolves in the ocean: about 30 percent of the carbon dioxide people have added has entered the ocean, forming carbonic acid. Since 1750, surface-ocean pH has dropped by about 0.1, a roughly 30 percent increase in acidity, which reduces carbonate ion availability for corals and other shell-building organisms. Commercial greenhouses sometimes enrich CO2 under controlled water, nutrient, pest, and temperature conditions; that practice is not a planetary experiment and does not show that unbounded atmospheric CO2 is harmless. NASA-linked research also finds that land ecosystems have become less efficient at absorbing additional CO2 over recent decades as other limits bite. Extra 'plant food' does not remove heat-trapping, sea-level, or ocean-acidification harms.
questions: Do plants use CO2 in photosynthesis, so extra CO2 can enhance growth under some conditions?
Does greenhouse CO2 fertilization prove that rising atmospheric CO2 is harmless to climate and oceans?
Has the ocean absorbed a substantial fraction of human-emitted CO2, lowering surface pH?
Is CO2 a heat-trapping greenhouse gas whose industrial-era rise is central to recent warming?
Are CO2 fertilization benefits on land unlimited by water, nutrients, and heat stress?

articles.title: Stratospheric aerosol injection is a proposed cooling mask, not a CO2 cleanup or a substitute for mitigation
articles.text: Stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) is a proposed solar radiation modification (SRM) method: introducing aerosols into the stratosphere to reflect a fraction of incoming sunlight and temporarily cool the surface, analogous in part to sulfate aerosols after large volcanic eruptions. The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo is commonly cited as producing about 0.5°C of global cooling for up to a few years. IPCC-linked assessments treat SAI as the most-researched SRM option and note that, in models, it could limit warming, but imperfectly and with regional side effects. SRM does not remove carbon dioxide and does not stop ocean acidification; it would mask some warming while greenhouse-gas concentrations remain high. A sudden, sustained stop of a large SAI program while CO2 stayed elevated could produce rapid warming (termination shock). Governance concerns include uneven regional effects and the possibility of unilateral deployment. SAI research and tiny proposed experiments such as SCoPEx are not the same thing as operational geoengineering, and they are not evidence of a secret global spraying program.
questions: Is SAI a proposed method that would scatter sunlight using stratospheric aerosols, analogous in part to volcanic sulfate?
Would SAI by itself remove CO2 from the air or stop ocean acidification?
Did the 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption produce temporary global cooling of about 0.5°C?
Does IPCC-linked assessment treat SRM as a full replacement for cutting emissions rather than, at most, a supplement?
Could an abrupt stop of large-scale SAI, if CO2 remained high, produce rapid warming?

articles.title: Net zero is a carbon-budget accounting goal, not a claim that climate physics stops on pledge day
articles.text: In IPCC language, halting long-term global warming requires that human CO2 emissions reach net zero: remaining residual emissions balanced by removals, so that no additional CO2 is added to the atmosphere. The IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C found that pathways with no or limited overshoot of 1.5°C show global net anthropogenic CO2 emissions declining by about 45% from 2010 levels by 2030 (40–60% interquartile range) and reaching net zero around 2050 (2045–2055 interquartile range). Pathways likely to limit warming to below 2°C generally reach net-zero CO2 later, around 2070. Net zero is not a requirement that every activity emit absolutely zero CO2 with no offsets or removals, and a political pledge does not by itself stop warming if emissions continue. The Paris Agreement invites long-term low-emission strategies and is described by the United Nations as marking a shift toward a net-zero emissions world. Meeting net zero still requires deep cuts across energy, industry, land use and other greenhouse gases, not SAI or accounting tricks alone.
questions: Does IPCC assessment say global net-zero CO2 is required to stabilize long-term warming?
In SR15 1.5°C no/limited-overshoot pathways, do CO2 emissions reach net zero around mid-century?
Does net zero mean every factory and farm must emit absolutely zero CO2 with no carbon removals?
Do those 1.5°C pathways also show deep CO2 cuts by 2030, on the order of about 45% from 2010 levels?
Does announcing a net-zero target automatically stop warming regardless of actual emissions?

articles.title: Extreme-weather attribution: changing odds and intensity, not a single-cause slogan
articles.text: Event attribution asks how human-caused climate change altered the likelihood or intensity of a defined extreme, compared with a cooler pre-industrial climate — not whether an event had only one cause. IPCC AR6 Working Group I (Chapter 11 and FAQ 11.3) assesses that many extremes have become more probable and more intense, and that many of those changes can be attributed to human influence, with particularly strong evidence for heatwaves. World Weather Attribution (WWA), formed in 2014, frames rapid studies around intensity, likelihood, and pre-existing vulnerability. WWA states that climate change is worsening many extremes but that studies sometimes find no increase in likelihood or intensity for a given event type and region; those null results still inform disaster-risk reduction. WWA also states that every heatwave is now made stronger and more likely by human-caused climate change. The first peer-reviewed event-attribution study is commonly cited as Stott et al. (2004), which found that climate change had at least doubled the risk of the 2003 European summer heatwave. Tornadoes and some other hazards remain harder to attribute than heat.
questions: Does event attribution typically estimate how climate change changed an event's likelihood or intensity rather than naming a single cause?
Has IPCC assessed that human influence has increased the probability and intensity of many heat extremes?
Do attribution studies find that climate change makes every type of extreme more likely in every region?
Was the 2003 European heatwave among the first events shown in the peer-reviewed literature to have had its risk increased by climate change?
According to World Weather Attribution, is every heatwave now made stronger and more likely by human-caused climate change?

articles.title: ClimateFEVER polar-bear claims: SUPPORTS extinction-risk wording, REFUTES a simple 'population is growing' slogan
articles.text: CLIMATE-FEVER (Diggelmann et al., 2020) is a FEVER-style dataset of 1,535 real-world climate claims collected from the internet, each paired with five Wikipedia evidence sentences (7,675 pairs total). Claim-level labels are SUPPORTS, REFUTES, NOT_ENOUGH_INFO, or DISPUTED from evidence majority vote. The public Hugging Face copy is tdiggelm/climate_fever (1,535-row test split). In the documented 40-row slice from that hub, claim_id 0 is 'Global warming is driving polar bears toward extinction' labeled SUPPORTS, and claim_id 6 is 'The polar bear population has been growing.' labeled REFUTES. Those labels are annotations over retrieved Wikipedia sentences, not a new aerial survey. They align with independent scientific sources: polar bears depend on sea ice, IUCN lists the species as Vulnerable with sea-ice loss as the primary long-term threat, and a blanket claim of global population growth is not a supported summary. A SUPPORTS label on extinction-risk wording is not a claim that polar bears are already extinct tomorrow; a REFUTES label on 'the population has been growing' is not a claim that no local count ever rose.
questions: In ClimateFEVER, is the claim that global warming is driving polar bears toward extinction labeled SUPPORTS?
In ClimateFEVER, is the claim that the polar bear population has been growing labeled REFUTES?
Does ClimateFEVER attach five Wikipedia evidence sentences to each claim?
Is a ClimateFEVER SUPPORTS label an evidence-majority annotation, not a substitute for a new field census?
Does ClimateFEVER's REFUTES label on 'the polar bear population has been growing' mean polar bears are already globally extinct?

articles.title: ClimateFEVER CO2 claims: the modern rise is not ocean degassing, and greenhouse generators are not a planetary disproof
articles.text: Two widely circulated CO2 talking points appear in CLIMATE-FEVER (Diggelmann et al., 2020) and in the documented Hugging Face slice of tdiggelm/climate_fever. Claim_id 10 says human additions of CO2 are within measurement error and that the gradual increase is mainly oceans degassing as Earth emerges from the last ice age; ClimateFEVER labels it REFUTES. Claim_id 19 says that if CO2 were terrible, installing a CO2 generator in a greenhouse would kill the plants; ClimateFEVER labels it REFUTES. Those annotations match physical carbon-cycle evidence. NASA notes that the recent atmospheric CO2 rise is mainly from human activity (fossil fuels and land-use change) and that about 30 percent of that carbon has entered the ocean, which is a net sink, not the main source of the industrial-era increase. Surface-ocean pH has fallen by about 0.1 since 1750. Greenhouse CO2 enrichment can aid some crops under controlled conditions; it does not imply that unbounded atmospheric CO2 is harmless, nor that CO2 is 'not a pollutant' in the climate sense. Human CO2 additions are far larger than the uncertainty of the Mauna Loa / global CO2 record.
questions: Does ClimateFEVER refute the claim that the modern CO2 rise is mainly oceans degassing after the last ice age?
Are human fossil-fuel CO2 additions small enough to sit inside the error of the atmospheric CO2 record?
Does ClimateFEVER refute the greenhouse-generator argument as proof that atmospheric CO2 cannot harm the planet?
Has the ocean been a net sink for a large share of anthropogenic CO2 rather than the main source of the recent rise?
Does using extra CO2 in commercial greenhouses disprove the greenhouse effect of CO2 in the open atmosphere?

articles.title: Global sea level is rising from warming oceans and land ice, not a stalled or purely pre-industrial constant
articles.text: NOAA Climate.gov reports that global mean sea level has risen about 8–9 inches (21–24 centimeters) since 1880. The rise is mostly meltwater from glaciers and ice sheets plus thermal expansion of seawater as it warms; a smaller term is land-water storage change such as groundwater depletion. In 2023, global mean sea level was 101.4 millimeters (3.99 inches) above 1993 levels, the highest annual average in the satellite altimeter record that begins in 1993. NASA's sea-level portal cites a satellite-era rate of about 3.34 mm per year (1993–2020), compared with a slower 20th-century tide-gauge rate (about 1.56 mm per year for 1900–2018 in Frederikse et al. 2020 as tabulated by NASA). Melting of land-based ice adds water to the ocean. Melting of floating ice has a much smaller direct effect than land ice. Claims that sea-level rise 'is not going to happen' or that the satellite-era rate is slower than the 20th century contradict this observational record.
questions: Has global mean sea level risen on the order of 21–24 cm since 1880?
Are thermal expansion of warming seawater and melt of land ice the main drivers of the recent rise?
Is the satellite-era global mean sea-level rate slower than the 20th-century tide-gauge average?
Does melting of land-based glaciers and ice sheets add water that raises global sea level?
Does the observational record show that global sea-level rise is not occurring?

articles.title: Volcanoes emit CO2, but present-day volcanic CO2 is a small fraction of human emissions
articles.text: A recurring climate talking point is that volcanoes emit more carbon dioxide than human activities. The U.S. Geological Survey states that this is false. Published estimates of present-day subaerial plus submarine volcanic CO2 lie between about 0.13 and 0.44 billion metric tons (gigatons) per year. USGS notes that human activities were responsible for a projected 35 gigatons of CO2 in 2010 — about 80 to 270 times the volcanic range — and that present-day volcanoes release less than one percent of the CO2 released by human activities. Gerlach (2011, Eos) reaches the same qualitative conclusion. Large explosive eruptions can inject sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere and cause temporary cooling of the lower atmosphere; USGS states that carbon dioxide from contemporary eruptions has never caused detectable global warming. Volcanoes matter for Earth's long-term carbon cycle, but they do not explain the industrial-era CO2 rise and are not a disproof of anthropogenic warming.
questions: Do present-day volcanoes emit less than one percent of current human CO2 emissions according to USGS?
Were anthropogenic CO2 emissions around 2010 on the order of 35 gigatons, tens to hundreds of times volcanic estimates?
Has contemporary volcanic CO2 caused a detectable global warming signal that outweighs human emissions?
Can large explosive eruptions inject sulfate aerosols that temporarily cool the lower atmosphere?
Does the volcanic-CO2 comparison imply that humans emit negligible carbon compared with volcanoes?

articles.title: Great Barrier Reef mass bleaching is a marine-heat signal, not a one-off runoff-only event
articles.text: Mass coral bleaching occurs when heat stress causes corals to expel symbiotic algae. On the Great Barrier Reef, marine heatwaves have driven repeated mass bleaching, including major events in 1998, 2002 and 2016, with further mass bleaching in later summers. CLIMATE-FEVER claim_id 14, 'The Great Barrier Reef is experiencing the most widespread bleaching ever recorded', is labeled SUPPORTS in the documented tdiggelm/climate_fever slice; Wikipedia evidence sentences used by that dataset describe 2016 bleaching as more widespread than previously thought and as among the most severe recorded at that time. Elevated ocean temperature is a primary driver of those mass events. Other pressures — including runoff, water quality, and crown-of-thorns starfish outbreaks — also affect the Reef, so bleaching is not a claim that temperature is the only local stressor. Nor does a mass-bleaching year mean every coral on the Reef has permanently died: some colonies bleach and recover, while repeated heat events increase mortality and reduce recovery time. Treating bleaching solely as arson, runoff, or a hoax contradicts the temperature-linked observational record.
questions: Did ClimateFEVER label as SUPPORTS the claim that the Great Barrier Reef was experiencing the most widespread bleaching then recorded?
Is mass coral bleaching on the Reef linked to elevated ocean temperatures?
Have multiple mass bleaching events been documented on the Reef rather than a single unique year?
Is runoff the only environmental pressure, with no role for warming seas?
Does a mass-bleaching event mean every coral on the Reef has already permanently died?
